item.title: Now: cumulative knowledge
item.description:
Environmental knowledge keeps getting reset. A new survey, a new map or a new project arrives, and the last one is quietly replaced, along with everything it cost and everything it knew.

We’re working on the opposite: updating what is known as new data arrives, so that knowledge accumulates and uncertainty falls with each round instead of starting over. In Limpopo, South Africa, a continental soil survey is used to update regional soil fertility maps into domains that support land-use decisions.

(Under production)

item.title: Soil keys in your language
item.description:
Soil classification keys in Farsi, Kiswahili and the South African system, built with soil scientists who speak those languages. Language matters as much as the logic: a key is only useful if people can read it in their own words.

item.title: Integrated Soil Profile Mapping (Southern Africa)
item.description:
Soil properties mapped consistently with depth across Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa, so that maps no longer jump at every layer boundary. Sampling was sparse, only two horizons were sampled per profile, and the environmental gradients were extreme, so we developed a new method for the project: Integrated Soil Profile Mapping (ISPM). It builds on our earlier physics-informed depth spline (phySpline) and is now being extended to update existing soil maps and support decisions. See Now: cumulative knowledge.

Preprint: Integrated soil profile mapping reveals regional patterns of soil condition across Southern African agricultural lands
